options.b: The topography and intensity of problem behavior
options.c: A diagnosis that explains the behavior
options.d: Punishers that will stop the behavior

distractorExplanations.b: Topography and intensity describe what the behavior looks like and how strong it is; an FBA seeks why it continues (maintaining variables).
distractorExplanations.c: Diagnosis is not the goal of an FBA; it identifies environmental variables maintaining the behavior.
distractorExplanations.d: An FBA identifies function to build function-based interventions, not punishers to suppress behavior.

options.a: The learner's diagnosis and IQ score
options.b: Topography and duration of the behavior
options.c: The reinforcement schedule written into the behavior plan
options.d: Setting, people, materials, time of day

distractorExplanations.c: A reinforcement schedule is a programmed contingency in the plan, not an ecological variable such as setting, people, or time of day.
distractorExplanations.a: Diagnosis and IQ are client characteristics, not ecological variables in the environment.
distractorExplanations.b: Topography and duration describe the behavior itself, not the surrounding ecological context.

options.a: An independent opportunity first, then a prompt
options.c: A gestural prompt, then adds help
options.d: A fixed time delay of 4 seconds

distractorExplanations.a: Giving an independent opportunity first and then prompting is least-to-most prompting, the opposite order of most-to-least.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding help after a gesture is least-to-most; most-to-least starts with the most intrusive prompt.
distractorExplanations.d: Time delay is a separate prompting procedure; most-to-least starts with full assistance and fades.
